interface.name: gnoblin_session_host_v1

description.summary: the host compositor's channel to one hosted session

interface.description:
Offered only on the connection the host compositor brokered for one hosted session: the compositor marks that connection before its first request, so a greeter, an application, or a session's own clients never see this global at all. One object exists per session connection, and a second bind on the same connection is a protocol error.
The host is the server and the session is the client. The session's Gnoblin runs on the nested backend, so its outputs are surfaces of this connection and its clients are its own.
The two sides divide the host's invariants like this:
- The host hides the session's surfaces and paints the cover itself, so a session can never be shown by accident. It answers the manager only after a frame without the session reached every output. - The session covers its own scene and acknowledges with `protected` only once that cover was presented on its own outputs. A session that is asked to protect itself and then crashes leaves the host's cover standing and nothing is revealed.
Nothing here is a request the compositor performs on its own authority. `lock`, `logout` and `power` are published to the session manager as objects it may claim and answer; the compositor never locks, ends a session or calls logind because a client asked.

description.summary: what the session asked the machine to do

entry.name: already_bound
entry.summary: a second session host on one connection

entry.name: stale_protection
entry.summary: acknowledged a protection that was never requested

entry.name: invalid_hint
entry.summary: an output hint with a non-positive size or scale

entry.name: invalid_power_action
entry.summary: a power action outside the enum

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the session stops speaking this protocol

request.description: The protection state is kept: destroy is not a release, and a session that destroys its object while protected leaves the cover in place.

request.name: ready
request.description: Sent once the session serves its own clients and its shell is up. The host publishes it to the session manager, which is what decides whether to show the session, so readiness is a statement about the session and never a request to be shown. A second `ready` on the same object is harmless: readiness is a level, not an edge.

request.name: protected

description.summary: the cover for this protection was presented

request.description: The answer to `protect`. Send it only after the frame carrying the cover reached every output of the session: a cover that is merely committed proves nothing, because a flip already in flight can still show the desktop. A serial older than the current protection is ignored; a serial the host never sent is the `stale_protection` error.

request.name: lock

description.summary: ask for the session to be locked

request.description: A lock source inside the session - idle, a hotkey, a shell action. The host publishes it to the session manager as a request; whether the seat locks is the manager's decision and this request carries no consent.

request.name: logout

description.summary: ask for the session to end

request.description: The session asks to log out. As with `lock`, the manager decides, and the compositor never ends the session itself.

request.name: power

description.summary: ask for a machine power action

request.description: Reboot, power off, suspend or hibernate, published to the manager as a request. A nested session never calls logind: it does not own the seat, the hardware or the machine's policy. An action outside the enum is the `invalid_power_action` error.

request.name: output_hint

description.summary: how one of the session's outputs wants to be shown

request.description: A hint, sent once per output the session drives, then completed by `output_hint_done`. The host places the session's surfaces itself and may ignore the hint entirely; what it does with it is report it to the manager and use it to choose a size when the manager asks it to fit the session to an output. `name` is the session's own output name, `width` and `height` are logical pixels and `scale` is 24.8 fixed point. Hints sent between one `output_hint_done` and the next replace each other; the completed set replaces the previous set as a whole.

request.name: output_hint_done
request.description: Marks the end of a consistent set of `output_hint` requests, so a host never acts on a half-updated layout. Send it even when the set is empty, which says the session drives no output.

event.name: protect
event.description: The host is about to remove this session from its outputs and wants the session to cover its own scene as well, so a capture, a screenshot or a stale buffer of the session cannot show what the host just hid. Answer with `protected` and the same serial once the cover frame is presented. A protection already in place is not asked for twice.

event.name: unprotect
event.description: The host is showing this session again, so the cover the session raised for the last `protect` must go. Only the host can ask for this: a session cannot unprotect itself, which is what makes the manager's protection state the only way a session becomes visible.

event.name: closed

description.summary: the host is ending this hosted session
